subject: contact lens
title: What If You Never Took Out Your Contact Lenses?

scenes.text: What if you never took your contacts out, even to sleep? Your eyes would run short of air.
Your cornea has no blood vessels. It takes its oxygen from the air, through your tears.
Close your eyes and that supply already drops. A lens on top adds one more barrier.
The CDC says sleeping in lenses raises the risk of eye infection six to eight times.
Every year, about 18 to 20 of every 10,000 people who sleep in lenses get an infection of the cornea.
In one CDC report, a man wore soft lenses overnight on a hunting trip. He needed a new cornea.

description:
What if you never took your contact lenses out? Sleeping in them raises the risk of eye infection six to eight times, according to the CDC.
About a third of the 45 million American lens wearers say they sleep or nap in them. Each year 18 to 20 of every 10,000 overnight wearers develop microbial keratitis, and in a 2018 CDC case series most patients were left with permanent eye damage. Follow your eye doctor's advice.
